title: Unit output and prefix conversion policy
keywords: unit output SI prefix micro milli nano centimeter millimeter ohm degree percent ASCII final_unit
text:
Use SI units unless the problem explicitly asks for a different target unit. Keep final_unit ASCII only.
Common conversions: u=micro=1e-6, m=milli=1e-3, n=nano=1e-9, p=pico=1e-12, cm=1e-2 m, mm=1e-3 m, min=60 s, h=3600 s.
Use 'ohm' not Ω. Use 'm/s^2' not m/s². Use 'N/C' for electric field; 'V/m' is equivalent but prefer 'N/C' unless gold/unit asks otherwise. For percent, compute numeric percent and final_unit='%'.
Always print exactly json.dumps({"answer": final_answer, "unit": final_unit}).

title: SymCode style and helper pattern
keywords: symcode format json sympy final_answer final_unit deterministic helper norm vector matrix solve
text:
Every generated solution should be short deterministic Python:
import json
import sympy as sp
Define values with unit conversions first, then formulas, then final_answer=float(...), final_unit='...'.
For vectors, use sp.Matrix and helper:
def norm(v): return sp.sqrt(v.dot(v))
For equations with one positive unknown, use sp.symbols(..., positive=True), sp.solve, then select the positive real solution.
Do not include explanations in code. Do not read files or use unsafe imports.

title: Common physical constants
keywords: constant g Coulomb k epsilon0 pi speed sound standard physics constants
text: If the problem gives a constant, use the given value. Otherwise common defaults: Coulomb k≈9e9 N*m^2/C^2, epsilon0≈8.854e-12 F/m, g≈9.8 m/s^2 or 10 m/s^2 only if the problem says so. Use sp.pi for pi. For sound speed, use the value given in the problem.

title: Capacitor charge voltage energy
keywords: capacitor capacitance charge voltage energy stored Q C U V electric field energy
text:
Use when a problem asks for capacitor charge, capacitance, voltage, or stored energy.
Core formulas: Q=C*U, C=Q/U, U=Q/C, W=1/2*C*U^2 = Q^2/(2*C) = 1/2*Q*U.
Convert uF to F, mC/uC/nC to C. Output energy in J, capacitance in F, charge in C unless another target unit is requested.

title: Capacitors in series or parallel
keywords: capacitors connected series parallel equivalent capacitance charge voltage battery
text:
Series capacitors: 1/Ceq=sum(1/Ci); all capacitors store the same charge Q=Ceq*U_total; voltages split as Ui=Q/Ci.
Parallel capacitors: Ceq=sum(Ci); all capacitors have the same voltage U; charge on each Qi=Ci*U; total charge Q_total=Ceq*U.
Convert capacitances to F before computing.

title: Parallel plate capacitor and uniform field
keywords: parallel plate capacitor area distance dielectric epsilon surface charge density electric field voltage
text: Parallel plate capacitor: C=epsilon0*epsilon_r*A/d. Uniform field between plates: E=U/d. For surface charge density sigma on two large opposite plates, field between plates is E=sigma/epsilon0 and approximately zero outside. For one infinite sheet, E=sigma/(2*epsilon0) on each side.

title: Ohm law, power, and electrical energy
keywords: resistor resistance current voltage power energy Ohm Joule heat circuit
text:
Ohm law: U=I*R. Power: P=U*I=I^2*R=U^2/R. Electrical energy: W=P*t=U*I*t=I^2*R*t=U^2*t/R.
For time, convert minutes/hours to seconds when output energy in J. For RMS AC power in a pure resistor or resonant RLC, use P=U_rms^2/R.

title: Resistors in series and parallel
keywords: resistors series parallel equivalent resistance total current voltage source
text:
Series resistors: Req=sum(Ri), same current I=U/Req.
Parallel resistors: 1/Req=sum(1/Ri), or for two resistors Req=R1*R2/(R1+R2). Total current from source I=U/Req. Branch currents Ii=U/Ri.

title: Resistance of a uniform conductor
keywords: conductor resistance resistivity length cross sectional area rho S wire ohm mm2 m
text: Uniform conductor: R = rho*l/S. Be careful with resistivity units. If rho is in ohm*mm^2/m and S is in mm^2, R = rho*l/S directly. If converting to SI, ohm*mm^2/m = 1e-6 ohm*m and mm^2 = 1e-6 m^2; the factors cancel consistently.

title: Inductor energy, induced EMF, and reactance
keywords: inductor inductance coil solenoid magnetic field energy induced emf current changes uniformly reactance frequency
text: Inductor magnetic energy: W=1/2*L*I^2. Induced EMF magnitude for uniform current change: |e|=L*|Delta I|/Delta t. Inductive reactance: X_L=omega*L=2*pi*f*L. Output units: J, V, or ohm. Long solenoid magnetic field: B = mu0*n*I, where n is turns per meter and mu0=4*pi*1e-7 T*m/A.

title: LC oscillation energy and resonance frequency
keywords: LC circuit resonant frequency electric energy magnetic energy cos sin omega capacitance inductance
text: LC resonant angular frequency: omega=1/sqrt(L*C), f=1/(2*pi*sqrt(L*C)). Total energy is conserved: W_total = W_electric + W_magnetic. If W_C = A*cos^2(omega*t), then W_total=A and W_L=A-W_C=A*sin^2(omega*t).

title: Series AC RLC impedance and power
keywords: AC RLC impedance resistance inductive reactance capacitive reactance power RMS frequency doubled
text: Series AC RLC: Z=sqrt(R^2+(X_L-X_C)^2), I=U/Z, power dissipated in R: P=I^2*R=U^2*R/Z^2. If frequency changes by factor k, X_L becomes k*X_L0 and X_C becomes X_C0/k. At resonance, X_L=X_C and Z=R.

title: RLC resonance with current ratio after frequency change
keywords: RLC resonance current halved frequency doubled inductive reactance capacitive reactance unknown XL0 XC0 impedance
text:
At resonance in a series RLC circuit: X_L0=X_C0=X and Z0=R. If frequency changes by factor k=f/f0, then X_L=k*X and X_C=X/k. New impedance Z=sqrt(R^2+(k*X-X/k)^2). If voltage is unchanged, I_new/I0=Z0/Z. For current halved, set Z=2*R and solve for positive X. Output X as the inductive reactance at resonance in ohm.
SymCode pattern:
R=sp.Float(...); k=sp.Float(...); X=sp.symbols('X', positive=True)
Z_new=sp.sqrt(R**2+(k*X-X/k)**2)
sol=sp.solve(sp.Eq(Z_new, 2*R), X)
X0=[s for s in sol if s.is_real and s>0][0]

title: Two AC segments with LC omega squared condition and quadrature voltages
keywords: AC circuit two segments AM MB R1 capacitor R2 inductor LC omega squared quadrature power total voltage
text: Use for a series circuit with segment AM=(R1 in series with C), segment MB=(R2 in series with L), condition L*C*omega^2=1, and voltages u_AM and u_MB in quadrature. Then X_L=X_C=X and total impedance is purely resistive: Z_total=R1+R2. Quadrature condition gives X^2=R1*R2 but total power only needs P=U^2/(R1+R2) when total RMS voltage U is given.

title: Ideal transformer voltage and turns ratio
keywords: transformer primary secondary turns voltage current ideal N1 N2 U1 U2
text: Ideal transformer voltage ratio: U2/U1=N2/N1. Current ratio for ideal transformer: I2/I1=N1/N2. Power approximately conserved: U1*I1≈U2*I2. Use RMS values if AC.

title: Coulomb force between two point charges
keywords: Coulomb force two point charges separated distance magnitude k q1 q2
text: For two point charges separated by distance r, force magnitude F=k*abs(q1*q2)/r^2. Convert uC/nC/cm to SI. Use k given by the problem if provided; otherwise use about 9e9. Output unit N.

title: Net Coulomb force with vector components
keywords: net electric force point charges q1 q2 q3 force acting vector resultant triangle midpoint perpendicular bisector
text:
Use when asking for net electric force on a target charge from multiple source charges. Do not add magnitudes directly unless all forces are collinear. Use coordinates and vector sum.
Formula for force on target due to source: F = k*q_source*q_target*(r_target-r_source)/|r_target-r_source|^3. The sign of charges is included; the vector points automatically.
SymCode pattern:
def norm(v): return sp.sqrt(v.dot(v))
def coulomb_force_on_target(q_source, r_source, q_target, r_target):
    r_vec = r_target - r_source
    r = norm(r_vec)
    return k*q_source*q_target*r_vec/r**3
F_net = F1 + F2 + ...
F_mag = norm(F_net)
Output unit N.

title: Electric field from one point charge
keywords: electric field strength point charge distance magnitude E k q r N/C V/m
text: For one point charge, electric field magnitude at distance r is E=k*abs(q)/r^2. Direction is away from positive charge and toward negative charge. Output unit N/C or V/m as requested. In a dielectric medium with relative permittivity epsilon_r, use E = k*abs(q)/(epsilon_r*r^2). If field is directed toward the charge, q is negative; if away, q is positive.

title: Net electric field from point charges as vectors
keywords: net electric field point charges vector components midpoint perpendicular bisector square rectangle N/C V/m
text:
Use when asking for electric field at a point due to one or more point charges. Electric field does NOT multiply by the test charge. Use coordinates and sum vectors.
Formula: E = k*q_source*(r_point-r_source)/|r_point-r_source|^3.
SymCode pattern:
def norm(v): return sp.sqrt(v.dot(v))
def electric_field(q_source, r_source, r_point):
    r_vec = r_point - r_source
    r = norm(r_vec)
    return k*q_source*r_vec/r**3
E_net = E1 + E2 + ...
E_mag = norm(E_net)
Output unit N/C.

title: Electric potential from point charges
keywords: electric potential voltage point charge scalar sum k q over r volts
text: Electric potential is scalar: V = sum(k*q_i/r_i). Keep charge signs. Do not use vector components for potential. Work or energy moving charge q through potential difference U: W=q*U. Output V or J as requested.

title: Unknown charge from zero net electric field
keywords: net electric field equals zero find charge q1 q2 distances point M resultant E zero
text: Use when an unknown charge is found from E_net=0 at a point. Set coordinates for charges and observation point, compute each field vector E_i=k*q_i*(P-r_i)/|P-r_i|^3, sum components, and solve the component equation(s). If the geometry makes fields collinear, solve signed scalar fields along the line. Keep charge signs; the unknown can be positive or negative.

title: Electric field of large charged sheets or plates
keywords: wide parallel insulating plates sheets surface charge density sigma electric field between outside
text: For a single infinite sheet with surface charge density sigma: field magnitude on each side is sigma/(2*epsilon0). For two large parallel sheets with opposite densities +sigma and -sigma, fields add between the plates giving E=sigma/epsilon0 and cancel outside. For two identical same-sign sheets, fields cancel between the sheets and add outside. Use epsilon0 if sigma is numeric and no direct field value is given.

title: Electric field on axis of uniformly charged ring
keywords: thin circular ring uniformly charged radius total charge axis electric field center point xy plane z axis
text: Uniform charged ring of radius R and total charge Q. At a point on the axis a distance x from center: E = k*Q*x/(R^2+x^2)^(3/2). At center x=0, E=0. Output N/C.

title: Coordinates from three side lengths
keywords: triangle AB AC BC three distances coordinates point A B C vector force field
text:
For vector physics with distances AB, AC, BC, place A=(0,0), B=(AB,0). Then point C=(xC,yC): xC=(AC^2+AB^2-BC^2)/(2*AB), yC=sqrt(AC^2-xC^2). Use SI length units.
SymCode:
A=sp.Matrix([0,0]); B=sp.Matrix([AB,0])
xC=(AC**2+AB**2-BC**2)/(2*AB)
yC=sp.sqrt(AC**2-xC**2)
C=sp.Matrix([xC,yC])

title: Equilateral triangle coordinates
keywords: equilateral triangle three vertices side length coordinates vector force field
text: For an equilateral triangle side a, use A=(0,0), B=(a,0), C=(a/2, sqrt(3)*a/2). This works for force/field at a vertex; choose the target vertex as needed.

title: Right triangle coordinates
keywords: right triangle right angled perpendicular sides coordinates vector charges field force
text: For a right triangle, place the right angle at A=(0,0), one leg along x-axis and the other along y-axis, e.g. B=(b,0), C=(0,c). If side lengths are named differently, map them carefully from the statement. Then use vector formulas for field/force.

title: Collinear points and midpoint coordinates
keywords: collinear midpoint between A B same line perpendicular bisector point M coordinates
text: For charges on a line with AB=d, place A=(-d/2,0), B=(d/2,0), midpoint M=(0,0). Or use A=(0,0), B=d, midpoint M=d/2 for scalar collinear problems. For a point on the perpendicular bisector at height h, use M=(0,h) with A=(-d/2,0), B=(d/2,0).

title: Square and rectangle coordinates
keywords: square rectangle vertices fourth vertex diagonal coordinates electric field charges corners
text: For square side a: A=(0,0), B=(a,0), C=(a,a), D=(0,a). For rectangle with AB=w and AD=h: A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h). Use the requested point/vertex and sum vector fields or forces.

title: Resultant of two vectors with angle
keywords: two forces angle between resultant magnitude law of cosines vector components
text: For two vectors magnitudes A and B with included angle theta, resultant magnitude R=sqrt(A^2+B^2+2*A*B*cos(theta)). Convert degrees to radians using sp.pi/180 if using trig. If directions are perpendicular, R=sqrt(A^2+B^2).

title: Constant acceleration kinematics
keywords: constant acceleration initial speed final speed distance time braking maximum height vertical motion
text: Kinematics with constant acceleration: s=v0*t+1/2*a*t^2, v=v0+a*t, v^2=v0^2+2*a*s. For braking to rest, use v=0 and acceleration sign carefully. For vertical throw maximum height, v=0 and h=v0^2/(2*g).

title: Work-energy theorem
keywords: work kinetic energy force distance final speed starts from rest net force
text: Work by constant net force over distance s: W=F*s. Work-energy theorem: W=Delta K=1/2*m*v^2-1/2*m*v0^2. If starts from rest, v=sqrt(2*F*s/m). Gravitational potential m*g*h can convert to kinetic energy if air resistance is neglected.

title: Elevator apparent weight
keywords: elevator accelerating upward downward normal force apparent weight mass g
text: For a person/object in elevator: upward acceleration a gives N=m*(g+a). Downward acceleration a gives N=m*(g-a). If moving at constant velocity, N=m*g. Use sign from the problem statement.

title: Average speed and trip segmentation
keywords: average speed distance time round trip fractions total time total distance speed km/h
text: Average speed = total distance / total time. For equal-distance outbound and return speeds v1 and v2, average speed over round trip is 2*v1*v2/(v1+v2). For segments by fractions of total time, total distance = sum(v_i * time_fraction_i * T). For segments by fractions of total distance, total time = sum(distance_fraction_i * D / v_i).

title: Relative motion, meeting, and return trips
keywords: two vehicles moving towards each other same arrival time return trip stop time distance AB speed
text: For two objects moving toward each other, closing speed is v1+v2 and distance=(v1+v2)*t. For same arrival time to a common point, set d1/v1=d2/v2. For a round trip with stop time, total_time = d/v_go + stop_time + d/v_return; solve for d.

title: River boat and ferry motion
keywords: boat river downstream upstream ferry across river current width drift resultant velocity
text: Downstream speed = v_boat_still + v_current. Upstream speed = v_boat_still - v_current. For a ferry crossing a river of width w, crossing time t=w/v_perpendicular. Drift along the bank = v_current*t if the boat aims straight across. Total path length can be sqrt(w^2+drift^2).

title: Distances increasing by a fixed amount each time interval
keywords: first hour each subsequent hour additional arithmetic progression total distance motorboat
text: If the distance in the first equal time interval is a1 and each subsequent interval increases by d, the total for n intervals is S=n/2*(2*a1+(n-1)*d). Use when a vehicle travels for many hours and each hour's distance forms an arithmetic sequence.

title: Dropped object with sound return delay
keywords: stone dropped cave sound heard after time depth speed of sound free fall
text: For a dropped object and delayed sound heard after total time T: fall time t_f=sqrt(2*h/g), sound time t_s=h/v_sound, and T=t_f+t_s. Solve for h>0. Use given sound speed and g.

title: Simple harmonic motion, spring, and pendulum patterns
keywords: simple harmonic motion SHM x cos amplitude maximum distance spring force mass angular frequency pendulum period
text: SHM position x=A*cos(omega*t+phi): amplitude is |A|. Maximum distance traveled in time interval can be reasoned from phase change Delta phi=omega*Delta t and path along oscillation between turning points. For force F=F0*cos(omega*t+phi) on mass m in SHM, displacement amplitude A=F0/(m*omega^2) when F is the restoring resultant magnitude. Spring static extension under effective acceleration: x=m*g_eff/k. Simple pendulum small-angle period T=2*pi*sqrt(l/g); if period gives length, l=g*(T/(2*pi))^2. For train rail-joint resonance with pendulum period T0 and train speed v, strongest oscillation occurs when rail joint passing period equals T0, so rail spacing d=v*T0. Convert km/h to m/s.

title: Heat, phase change, and ideal gas
keywords: heat temperature specific heat latent heat fusion gas pressure ideal gas law mole volume
text: Temperature change heat: Q=m*c*DeltaT. Phase change at constant temperature: Q=m*L. Ideal gas law: P*V=n*R*T, so P=n*R*T/V. Keep SI units: kg, J, K, m^3, Pa.

title: Thin lens image distance
keywords: converging lens focal length object distance image distance cm thin lens
text: Thin lens formula: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Solve di=1/(1/f-1/do). If the problem gives distances in cm and asks image distance, keep final answer in cm unless requested otherwise.

title: Tilted plane mirror viewing geometry
keywords: plane mirror tilted backward vertical floor person height see image maximum distance edge mirror alpha
text: Use for tilted plane mirror standing on floor, tilted backward by angle alpha from vertical, asking maximum distance a person of height h can stand from mirror edge and still see image. For this dataset pattern, distance d = h / tan(alpha). Convert alpha to radians. SymCode: d = h / sp.tan(alpha_rad). Output unit m.

title: Measurement uncertainty and relative error
keywords: measurement absolute error relative error percentage uncertainty least count ammeter reading
text: Absolute error is usually the stated uncertainty or least count/2 depending on the convention in the problem. Relative error = absolute_error/measured_value. Percentage relative error = relative_error*100. Output unit '%' for percentage.

title: Average speed for equal-distance round trip
keywords: average speed round trip same distance go return A to B B to A speed going returning total time distance AB km/h
text:
Use when an object travels the same distance out and back, possibly with a stop/rest time. Let D be one-way distance. Total moving time is D/v1 + D/v2. If total elapsed time includes a rest, subtract rest first. Average speed over moving+rest time is total distance divided by total elapsed time; average speed over moving time only is 2D/(D/v1+D/v2)=2*v1*v2/(v1+v2). SymCode pattern:
D = sp.symbols('D', positive=True)
t_moving = D/v_go + D/v_return
# if total time known with rest: solve Eq(t_moving + rest, total_time) for D
# average over full journey: v_avg = 2*D/total_time
Use consistent units, usually km and h for km/h problems.

title: Average speed from fractions of total time
keywords: average speed first quarter of total time next half final quarter time fractions speed total travel time
text:
Use when the trip is split by fractions of total time. Average speed equals weighted average by time fractions: v_avg = sum(frac_i*v_i). The total time cancels. SymCode pattern:
fractions = [sp.Rational(1,4), sp.Rational(1,2), sp.Rational(1,4)]
speeds = [v1, v2, v3]
v_avg = sum(f*v for f, v in zip(fractions, speeds))
Output in the same speed unit if all speeds share the same unit.

title: Average speed from fractions of total distance, solve unknown speed
keywords: average speed first one third total distance remaining distance unknown speed cyclist fraction distance entire journey
text:
Use when distance fractions are known. Time = sum(distance_fraction/v_i)*D, so 1/v_avg = sum(frac_i/v_i). If one segment speed is unknown, solve for it. SymCode pattern:
v = sp.symbols('v', positive=True)
eq = sp.Eq(1/v_avg, frac1/v1 + frac2/v)
sol = sp.solve(eq, v)[0]
Output in the speed unit used by the problem.

title: Find one-way distance from total time including rest
keywords: depart arrive stop rest return total time distance AB speed going speed returning hours minutes schedule
text:
Use for schedules such as depart at a clock time, rest for some duration, return with another speed, arrive at a later clock time. Convert clock times to elapsed hours. Equation: total_elapsed = D/v1 + rest_time + D/v2. SymCode pattern:
D = sp.symbols('D', positive=True)
eq = sp.Eq(D/v1 + rest + D/v2, total_elapsed)
D_value = sp.solve(eq, D)[0]
If the question asks distance AB, output D.

title: Two objects moving toward each other and meeting
keywords: two vehicles start from A and B moving towards each other meet after time distance AB car motorbike speed
text:
Use when two objects start from opposite ends and move toward each other. Closing speed is v1+v2. Distance between starting points: D=(v1+v2)*t. If one speed or time is unknown, solve the same equation. SymCode pattern:
D = (v1 + v2) * t
Use consistent units, e.g. km/h and hours gives km.

title: Same arrival time with different distances
keywords: same arrival time arrive at same time different distances moving towards common point C AC BC speed v1 v2
text: Use when two objects start at the same time from different locations and must arrive at a common point at the same time. Set d1/v1 = d2/v2 and solve for the unknown speed. This is not for opposite-direction meeting before arrival.

title: Piecewise distance with fractions of remaining distance
keywords: first hour covers fraction total distance second hour fraction remaining additional km third hour last remaining distance total in 3 hours
text:
Use when a trip distance D is covered in stages: first stage is a fraction of total D, next stage is a fraction of the remaining distance plus a fixed amount, final stage is the rest. Create symbolic D and track remaining distance after each stage. SymCode pattern:
D = sp.symbols('D', positive=True)
d1 = frac_total * D
rem1 = D - d1
d2 = frac_remaining * rem1 + extra
rem2 = rem1 - d2
# if third hour covers rem2 and speed/time condition exists, use it; if total time and speed asked, compute v_avg = D/total_time.
This card is for constructing the algebra, not for copying sample-specific numbers.

title: Constant acceleration from distance, time, and initial speed
keywords: initial speed travels distance in time constant acceleration calculate acceleration s ut half at squared
text:
Use when initial speed u, distance s, and time t are known under constant acceleration. Formula: s = u*t + 1/2*a*t^2, so a = 2*(s-u*t)/t^2. Other useful formulas: v = u+a*t, v^2 = u^2+2*a*s. SymCode pattern:
a = 2*(s - u*t)/t**2
Output unit: m/s^2 if s in m and t in s.

title: Braking distance with uniform deceleration
keywords: car brakes uniformly to rest initial speed acceleration negative braking distance stopping distance
text:
Use when an object slows from initial speed u to final speed v=0 with constant acceleration a<0. Formula: v^2 = u^2 + 2*a*s, so s = (v^2-u^2)/(2*a). SymCode pattern:
v = sp.Float(0)
s = (v**2 - u**2)/(2*a)
final_answer = float(abs(s))
Output length unit.

title: Vertical throw maximum height
keywords: ball thrown vertically upward initial speed maximum height g final speed zero
text:
Use when an object is thrown upward with initial speed u and asks maximum height. At the top v=0. Formula: h = u^2/(2*g). SymCode pattern:
h = u**2/(2*g)
Output meter if u in m/s and g in m/s^2.

title: Free fall height remaining from speed
keywords: dropped from height reaches speed height above ground neglect air resistance mass sphere free fall energy
text:
Use when an object is dropped from height H from rest and asks height above ground when speed is v. Distance fallen y satisfies v^2 = 2*g*y. Height above ground is H-y. SymCode pattern:
y = v**2/(2*g)
h_remaining = H - y
Mass cancels if air resistance is neglected.

title: Vertical ascent then descent piecewise motion
keywords: hot air balloon ascends vertically speed seconds then descends speed after seconds height above ground
text:
Use for vertical piecewise constant velocities. Height after ascent: h1 = v_up*t_up. During descent: h = h1 - v_down*t_down. Convert fractions like 5/9 m/s using sp.Rational(5,9). SymCode pattern:
h1 = v_up * t_up
h = h1 - v_down * t_down
Output meters.

title: Aircraft climb angle and vertical altitude
keywords: aircraft airplane ascending ascent climb flight path angle horizontal vertical altitude height sine speed time
text: Use only when an aircraft/airplane is ascending or climbing along a path that makes angle theta with the horizontal, and the problem asks vertical climb/altitude/height. Path distance s=v*t. Vertical component h=s*sin(theta). Convert units first. Not for mirror optics or ordinary road trips.

title: Distance from velocity-time function until stop
keywords: velocity v(t) linear function stops distance travels from t=0 until stops uniformly decelerated motion
text:
Use when velocity is given as v(t), often linear, and asks distance until stop. First solve v(t_stop)=0. Distance = integral of speed over time. If velocity remains nonnegative on interval, distance = integral v(t) dt. SymCode pattern:
t = sp.symbols('t', real=True)
v = v_expr
t_stop = sp.solve(sp.Eq(v, 0), t)[0]
s = sp.integrate(v, (t, 0, t_stop))
Output length unit matching v*time.

title: Distance traveled from position function
keywords: equation of motion x equals function of time position x-axis distance traveled after hours kilometers
text:
Use when position x(t) is given and asks distance traveled over a time interval. If velocity does not change sign, distance = abs(x(t2)-x(t1)). If velocity changes sign, split at roots of dx/dt. SymCode pattern:
t = sp.symbols('t', real=True)
x = x_expr
points = [t0, t1] + roots_inside_interval
distance = sum(abs(x.subs(t, points[i+1]) - x.subs(t, points[i])) for i in range(len(points)-1))
For x=5-20t from 0 to 2 h, velocity is always negative, so distance=abs(x(2)-x(0)).

title: Free fall last-second distance relation
keywords: dropped from rest last 1 second twice distance second immediately preceding free fall height time ground
text:
Use when free-fall distances in the final seconds are related. For drop from rest: s(t)=1/2*g*t^2. Distance in last 1 second before impact at total time T is s(T)-s(T-1). Distance in the preceding 1 second is s(T-1)-s(T-2). Set up the given ratio and solve for T, then height H=s(T). SymCode pattern:
T = sp.symbols('T', positive=True)
s = lambda x: sp.Rational(1,2)*g*x**2
d_last = s(T) - s(T-1)
d_prev = s(T-1) - s(T-2)
sol = sp.solve(sp.Eq(d_last, ratio*d_prev), T)
H = s(T_value)
Output meters.

title: River upstream/downstream distance with current speed
keywords: boat downstream upstream current speed still water distance AB time upstream downstream longer return
text:
Use for boat moving with and against current. If v is boat speed in still water and c is current speed, downstream speed is v+c and upstream speed is v-c. If the problem directly gives actual speed relative to bank, use that as ground speed. Equations: t_down = D/(v+c), t_up = D/(v-c). Use given time difference or total time to solve D or v. SymCode pattern:
D = sp.symbols('D', positive=True)
t_down = D/(v_boat + v_current)
t_up = D/(v_boat - v_current)
# solve Eq(t_up - t_down, delta_t) or Eq(t_up + stop + t_down, total_t).

title: Ferry crossing river with width and drift
keywords: river width ferry opposite bank point directly across current drift distance resultant velocity perpendicular banks
text:
Use for ferry crossing a river. Decompose velocity into across-river and along-river components. Crossing time t = width / v_across. Drift = v_current * t if boat aims straight across. If the landing point distance along opposite bank is given, use right triangle geometry or component equations. SymCode pattern:
t = width / v_across
drift = v_current * t
path = sp.sqrt(width**2 + drift**2)
Use meters/seconds or kilometers/hours consistently.

title: Basic speed, distance, and time
keywords: speed distance time travel cycling walking car how far km/h hours m/s v t s
text: Use for direct uniform motion asking distance, speed, or time. Formula: distance = speed*time, speed = distance/time, time = distance/speed. Keep units consistent: km/h with hours gives km; m/s with seconds gives m.

title: Round trip with clock times and rest stop
keywords: clock time depart departs departure arrive arrives arriving AM PM same day upon arriving stop stops rest duration returns return final arrival calculate distance AB round trip go back speed outbound inbound
text: Use when a car/vehicle departs at a clock time, travels from A to B, upon arriving stops/rests for a given duration, then returns to A with another speed and final arrival clock time. Convert clock times such as AM/PM to total elapsed hours. Equation: total_elapsed = D/v_go + stop_time + D/v_return. Solve D = (total_elapsed-stop_time)/(1/v_go + 1/v_return). Output distance in km if speeds are km/h.

title: Same path, different travel times, known speed difference
keywords: same path same distance travel times minutes slower per minute faster length path school field
text: Use when people travel the same distance D with different times and a speed difference is given. Speeds are v_i=D/t_i. If one person is d_speed slower per minute than another, set D/t_fast - D/t_slow = d_speed and solve for D. Use consistent time units, e.g. minutes and m/min.

title: Maximum distance traveled in SHM during a time interval
keywords: simple harmonic motion maximum distance travel time interval x cos omega t phase amplitude
text: For SHM x=A*cos(omega*t+phi), period T=2*pi/omega. Maximum path length over interval Delta_t: each half-period contributes 2A. Let n=floor(Delta_t/(T/2)), rem=Delta_t-n*T/2. Base distance = n*2A. Extra maximum during rem is at most 2A*sin(omega*rem/2) for rem<=T/2. For common case Delta_t=3T/4, maximum distance=3A. Output same unit as amplitude.

title: Train rail joints excite a pendulum by resonance
keywords: train rail joints jolted oscillates strongest pendulum period speed length rail segment distance between joints
text: Use when a pendulum in a train oscillates most strongly due to periodic jolts from rail joints. Resonance occurs when time between rail joints equals the natural period T0. Rail spacing d = v*T0. Convert v from km/h to m/s if output is meters.

title: Magnetic field inside a long solenoid
keywords: solenoid turns per meter n current magnetic field inside B mu0
text: For a long solenoid, magnetic field inside is B = mu0*n*I, where n is turns per meter, I is current, and mu0 = 4*pi*1e-7 T*m/A. Output unit T.

title: Point charge electric field in dielectric medium
keywords: dielectric medium dielectric constant relative permittivity electric field directed towards charge sign magnitude q
text: For a point charge in dielectric medium with relative permittivity epsilon_r, E = k*abs(q)/(epsilon_r*r^2). Thus abs(q)=E*epsilon_r*r^2/k. Direction: field points away from positive charge and toward negative charge. If the field at M is directed toward the charge, q is negative. Output C.

title: Foot of altitude from right angle to hypotenuse
keywords: right triangle foot of altitude vertex A hypotenuse H AB AC BC electric field force coordinates
text: Use when triangle ABC is right-angled at A and point H is the foot of altitude from A to hypotenuse BC. Set A=(0,0), B=(AB,0), C=(0,AC). Compute H by projecting A onto line BC: v=C-B; t=((A-B).dot(v))/(v.dot(v)); H=B+t*v. Then use vector field/force formulas at H.

title: Unknown charge from vector electric-field relation
keywords: unknown charge q1 q2 q3 vector electric field E2 E13 equal zero resultant solve rectangle square point D
text: Use when an unknown charge must be found from a vector relation between electric fields, e.g. E_net=0 or E2=E13 at a point. Build coordinates, define unknown q=sp.symbols(...), compute each field vector E_i=k*q_i*(P-r_i)/|P-r_i|^3, then solve component equation(s). Keep charge signs.

title: Spring oscillator when support accelerates from natural length
keywords: spring support moved downwards acceleration undeformed amplitude mass k g effective acceleration
text: Use when a mass on a vertical spring starts at the undeformed position and the support/frame accelerates. In the accelerating frame, effective gravity is g_eff = g - a if the support accelerates downward with acceleration a. New equilibrium extension x0 = m*g_eff/k. If released from natural length with zero relative velocity, oscillation amplitude A=x0. Output m.
